name: One item
why: 7: an item that fills the bag exactly fits.

name: Best value per kilogram goes wrong
why: 15. The small item has the better value per kilogram (2 against 1.5), but taking it leaves no room for the big one.

name: Two of the second best
why: 48: both 5s. Greedy by value per kilogram takes the 6 first and stops at 30.

name: Items worth nothing
why: 9: only the item worth 9 counts. Items worth 0 never change the best value.

name: Everything fits
why: 6: the bag holds every item, so take them all.

name: Thirty items
show: 30 random items of weight and value 1 to 1,000, a bag of 7,000
why: Trying all 2³⁰ choices, about a billion, is too slow. With the bound, about a hundred nodes are enough.

name: 100 items, values unrelated to weights
show: 100 items with random weights and values from 10⁸ to 10⁹; the bag holds half the total weight
why: Weights and values up to 10⁹, so a table by weight or by value is far too big. A bound that adds up every item left prunes almost nothing; the fractional bound needs under a thousand nodes.

name: 100 items, values near the weights
show: 100 items whose values differ from their weights by up to 10⁸; the bag holds half the total weight
why: Values within 10⁸ of the weights. The fractional bound still prunes well.

name: 60 items, every value 10⁸ above its weight
show: 60 items with value = weight + 10⁸; the bag holds half the total weight
why: A hard kind of instance for branch and bound: every item has almost the same value per kilogram, so bounds are close to each other. About 5,600 nodes here; some such instances need millions, which is why branch and bound has no fast guarantee.
